bib.title: Progressive Growing of GANs for Improved Quality, Stability, and Variation

read.skipped: Appendix G/H LSUN per-category figure pages (12-18) were skimmed for FID/SWD labels only; they are image galleries.

question: How can GANs be trained stably to generate high-resolution images (up to 1024x1024) with good quality and variation?
hypothesis: Growing the generator and discriminator progressively from low to high resolution gives an easier curriculum, so training is faster and more stable at high resolution.
contributions: Progressive growing of generator and discriminator with fade-in of new layers
Minibatch standard deviation layer to increase variation
Equalized learning rate and pixelwise feature vector normalization in the generator to limit signal-magnitude escalation
Sliced Wasserstein distance over Laplacian pyramid patches as a quality and variation metric

method.summary: A single GAN starts at 4x4 resolution and layers are added to G and D in mirrored fashion, each faded in with a linearly increasing residual weight alpha. Training uses WGAN-GP loss with Adam, no batch/layer normalization, equalized runtime weight scaling, pixelwise normalization in G and a parameter-free minibatch stddev feature map in D.

datasets.name: CELEBA-HQ
datasets.source: Built from the 202599 in-the-wild CELEBA images (Liu et al., 2015); released with the code
datasets.preprocessing: JPEG-artifact-removal autoencoder, 4x adversarial super-resolution, mirror padding and Gaussian filtering, landmark-based oriented crop, 4096x4096 bilinear then box filter to 1024x1024; best 30000 kept by a frequency-based quality metric; mirror augmentation in all CELEBA/CELEBA-HQ tests

datasets.name: LSUN (30 categories, 256x256)
datasets.size: 100k images per category; BEDROOM and DOG use all available data
datasets.preprocessing: mirror augmentation except BEDROOM and DOG; a separate network per category with identical parameters

models.name: Progressive GAN, CELEBA-HQ 1024x1024 (Table 2)
models.params: 23.1M trainable parameters for each of G and D
models.architecture: convolutional G and D, replicated 3-layer blocks (Conv 3x3, LReLU, Conv 3x3, LReLU, up/downsample), 4x4 base, 512 max feature maps
models.init_from: N(0,1) weights scaled at runtime by He constant; biases zero

other.minibatch_stddev: added as a 513th feature map at 4x4 near end of D

models.name: Low-capacity net for Sec 6.1 / Table 1
models.architecture: as above, halve feature maps at 16x16 and divide by 4 at subsequent resolutions, leaving 32 maps in the last Conv 3x3 layers

models.name: Gulrajani et al. (2017) WGAN-GP baseline config
models.architecture: ReLU, tanh last layer, batch norm in G, layer norm in D, He init, no progressive growth, no minibatch stddev, no runtime weight scaling

training.objective: WGAN-GP (also LSGAN in an alternate run) with n_critic=1; discriminator loss L' = L + eps_drift * E[D(x)^2], eps_drift = 0.001
training.lr_schedule: none: no learning rate decay or rampdown
training.batch_size: 16 for 4x4 to 128x128; 14 at 256x256; 6 at 512x512; 3 at 1024x1024 (64 in Gulrajani baseline; 16 in Table 1 (c) onward)
training.regularisation: pixelwise normalization in G; equalized learning rate; minibatch stddev; mirror augmentation; CIFAR10 WGAN-GP gamma=750
training.hardware: 8 Tesla V100 GPUs (CELEBA-HQ); single NVIDIA Tesla P100 for timing in Fig 4
training.seeds: CIFAR10 mean from 10 random initializations; MNIST mode test 8 random initializations; others null

other.schedule: train 4x4 until 800k real images shown, then alternate: fade in next block over 800k images, stabilize 800k images, repeat
other.generator_weight_average: exponential running average of G weights, decay 0.999, used for visualisation
other.lsgan_noise: multiplicative Gaussian noise on input of each Conv 3x3 and Conv 4x4 in D, magnitude 0.2*max(0, d_hat_t - 0.5)^2, d_hat_t = 0.1d + 0.9 d_hat_{t-1}
other.sec_6_1_stop: training stopped after discriminator shown 10M real images
other.adaptive_minibatch: minibatch size depends on current resolution to fit memory

inference.samples: SWD: 16384 random images, 128 descriptors per Laplacian level (2^21 per level); MS-SSIM: 10000 pairs of generated images; FID: 50K images

other.video_interpolation: randomize latent per frame, Gaussian blur across time sigma=45 frames @ 60Hz, normalize to hypersphere

metrics.name: Sliced Wasserstein distance (SWD)
metrics.definition: SWD between 7x7x3 patches (147-dim, channel-normalized) from Laplacian pyramid levels (16x16 up to full res) of training and generated images, 512 projections

metrics.name: MS-SSIM
metrics.definition: multi-scale structural similarity averaged over 10000 pairs of generated images (variation among outputs only)

metrics.name: Inception score (CIFAR10)
metrics.definition: standard inception score; best run, and mean over highest scores of 10 runs

metrics.name: FID
metrics.definition: Frechet Inception Distance (Heusel et al., 2017) from 50K images

metrics.name: MNIST-1K modes covered and KL
metrics.definition: number of 1000 discrete modes covered among 25,600 images; KL(histogram || uniform)

eval.protocol: Cumulative ablation (Table 1) on CELEBA and LSUN BEDROOM at 128x128 with truncated 10M-image training; visual comparison for LSUN; inception score best run vs mean of 10 runs; no significance test.

availability.weights: trained networks via Google Drive link in the paper

limits: Authors concede 'there is a long way to true photorealism': semantic sensibility and dataset-dependent constraints (e.g. straight vs curved objects) are poor, and micro-structure needs work.
Authors did not compare against other variation-increasing methods (unrolling, repelling regularizer, multiple generators), noting they may increase variation more or be orthogonal.
The gamma=750 WGAN-GP trick was tried only on CIFAR10, not other datasets.
LSGAN is less stable than WGAN-GP and tends to lose variation late in long runs; needs an adaptive noise hack.
Best-run CIFAR10 record 8.80 is a lucky run; 10-run mean is 8.56.
Speedup at 1024x1024 relies on extrapolation of the non-progressive curve to 520 h.
Table 1 ablation is cumulative and non-converged (10M images, reduced-capacity net), single run, no variance reported.
Number of training steps/iterations, precision and seeds for the main runs are not stated; no human evaluation; CELEBA-HQ has no held-out split.
Dated: GAN-based; FID on 50K images reported only in appendix figures; later work (StyleGAN) replaced the architecture, and diffusion models superseded GANs for image synthesis.

terms.definition: Start G and D at 4x4 resolution and add layers that model finer detail as training progresses, fading new layers in with a residual weight alpha rising linearly from 0 to 1.

Compute the standard deviation of each feature at each spatial location over the minibatch, average over features and locations to one value, and concatenate it as an extra constant feature map; no learnable parameters.
Initialize weights from N(0,1) and scale them at runtime by the per-layer He constant, w_hat = w/c, so all weights have the same dynamic range under Adam/RMSProp.
b = a / sqrt(mean_j (a_j)^2 + eps), eps=1e-8, applied per pixel after each Conv 3x3 in the generator.
SWD between Laplacian-pyramid patch sets of generated and training images, per scale starting from 16x16.
